paragraphs.text: Multi-engine web search & page fetching MCP server
PrismSearch
简体中文 | English
A multi-engine web search MCP (Model Context Protocol) server that aggregates search results from mu
ltiple search engines.
Like a prism splits light into a spectrum, PrismSearch disperses your search queries across multiple
engines for multi-perspective results.
### Why: web search for your AI agent, no search account required
The built-in web search of AI coding agents such as Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness usually depends
on an official account or a separately configured search API key. Use a third-party model, go throu
gh your own gateway, or simply skip the search account, and the built-in search is often unavailable
— the agent ends up coding "closed-book".
PrismSearch adds that capability back with one command:
- **No account, no API key out of the box**: the default engines (Bing, Baidu, …) scrape public resu
lt pages, so there is nothing to sign up for. Enable browser fetching (`fetcher.browser.enabled: tru
e`, requires Playwright) and Google works without a key too. Brave / Google API keys are picked up a

utomatically when present for extra reliability
- **Any model, any client**: plain MCP — works with

Claude Code, DeepSeek Harness, Cursor, VS Code, Cline and any other MCP-capable client
- **More than
search**: `fetch_page` reads web pages and PDFs (Markdown output, paginated for long documents), `w

echat_search` searches WeChat Official Account articles — the "found it, now read it" half
- **Works
behind restrictive networks**: Chinese sources (Baidu, Sogou, 360, WeChat) work out of the box; whe

n an engine is blocked or rate-limited the request falls back to the next one automatically
- **Clea
n results**: sponsored results injected by search engines are removed — see "Ad filtering" below
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> [!WARNING]
> Scraping engines fetch results from public web pages. You are responsible for complyi
ng with each search engine's and target site's terms of service, robots policies and local laws, and

for keeping request rates reasonable.
> The learning/research recommendation is not an additional r
estriction on the Apache-2.0 license. This project is not affiliated with any search engine company.
See the full Disclaimer at the end.
## Features
- **9 Search Sources**: Google, Bing, Baidu, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Yandex, Sogou, 360 Search, plus WeCh

at Official Account articles — with an extensible engine plugin system
- **5 MCP Tools**: `web_searc

h`, `image_search`, `fetch_page`, `wechat_search`, `list_engines`
- **Dual Transport**: stdio (local

) and Streamable HTTP (remote) MCP transport
- **Smart Engine Selection**: Auto-selects the best eng
ine based on availability, latency, success rate, and language matching, with cross-engine fallback
- **Google Triple Strategy**: Custom Search API → browser rendering → plain HTTP, with automatic fal

lback and sticky success memory
- **Ad Filtering**: Baidu promotions, Bing / Google / DuckDuckGo spo
nsored results and 360 / Sogou paid slots are dropped and don't eat into the requested count; anythi

ng that slips through is filtered again by its landing URL (paid-click tracking parameters)
- **Web
Page Fetching**: Fetch and extract content from URLs in HTML, plain text, or Markdown; optional Play

wright rendering for JS-heavy pages
- **Image Search**: Multi-engine image search with size/type fil

ters and optional base64 thumbnails
- **Caching**: Configurable TTL and LRU eviction with pluggable

backends — `cache.backend: sqlite | memory | redis` (SQLite by default)
- **Security**: SSRF protect

ion, rate limiting, domain whitelist/blacklist, optional Bearer auth for remote mode
- **Hot Reload*

*: Configuration file watching with automatic reload
- **Flexible Config**: YAML/JSON/TOML configura
tion with environment variable overrides
### Architecture
[代码示例省略，未执行]
In stdio mode there is a single client, so rate limiting happens at the tool layer; in HTTP mode the
transport rate-limits per client. Whether `fetch_page` is delegated to a worker is controlled by `w
orkers.useFor`; when no worker is available it falls back to the local fetchers, and the final URL r
eturned by a worker is SSRF-checked again.
## Requirements

- **Node.js ≥ 22.19**
- Native module `better-sqlite3` ships prebuilt binaries for mainstream platfo
rms (Windows/macOS/Linux, x64/arm64); if prebuilds are unavailable on your platform, a C++ build too

lchain is required
- **Optional**: Playwright for browser rendering. It is an `optionalDependency` —
installed by default (browsers download on install); use `npm install --omit=optional` for a minima
l install. To add it later: `npm install playwright && npx playwright install chromium`
### Privacy and local data
PrismSearch does not provide a hosted data service. In the default local stdio setup, requests and r
esponses pass through the local process; cache entries are stored locally (SQLite by default) and lo
gs go to the local process' stderr. If you enable remote HTTP transport, third-party API keys, brows
er fetching, proxies, Redis, or Workers, query text, URLs, headers, and fetched content may be sent
to those providers or services. Review their privacy policies and configure retention, access contro
ls, and `log.redact` for your deployment. Do not submit passwords, private tokens, personal data, or
confidential content unless you have verified every service in the path.
## Security
- **Auth**: in HTTP mode, binding to a non-loopback address requires auth (Bearer token or `X-API-Ke

y`), otherwise the server refuses to start; tokens are compared in constant time
- **Host / Origin c
hecks**: guard against DNS rebinding and cross-site requests; allow more with `server.allowedHosts`

/ `server.allowedOrigins`
- **Rate limiting**: per-client buckets in HTTP mode (credential fingerpri

nt or address); at the tool layer in stdio mode
- **SSRF guard**: `fetch_page` and workers only allo
w http/https, block private, loopback, link-local and other reserved addresses, re-check resolved ad

dresses at connect time (DNS rebinding), and check every redirect hop
- **Errors and logs**: errors
returned to clients pass through an allowlist and internal details go only to the log; logs redact q
uery strings and search terms by default
See SECURITY.md for how to report vulnerabilities.
